According to some gynaecologists, this section of the medical science has greatly improved particularly in the last ten years. Studies have been made and others are underway, and the findings are surprising. It is becoming always easier to treat all diseases affecting pregnant women.

Criminal Code
at least one member of the committee be a gynaecologist.
In this as in other areas of medical practice, the responsibility for appointments should be with the board charged with the control and management of the hospital. In our view, to require approval by the provincial College of Physicians and Surgeons would constitute an unwarranted reflection on the good faith and competence of the boards of hospitals which are either accredited or approved as defined in the bill. After all, we are dealing with hospitals that are accredited or approved. An accredited hospital, in the bill, means a hospital accredited by the Canadian Council on Hospital Accreditation, and an approved hospital means a hospital in a province approved by the minister of health of that province.
We believe that the qualification of the hospital by either the medical profession itself or by the provincial minister of health is sufficient to maintain the standard of professional conduct we believe is required for the purpose of the bill. -be amended by deleting paragraph (f) of subsection 6-

Clause 18 (6) (e) of the bill defines "therapeutic abortion committee" as follows:
"therapeutic abortion committee" for any hospital means a committee, comprised of not less than three members each of whom is a qualified medical practitioner, appointed by the board of that hospital for the purpose of considering and determining questions relating to terminations of pregnancy within that hospital.

-approved by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of the province concerned.
Why? Obviously because in our medical legislation the provisions differ from one province to another and that a certain latitude must therefore be provided.
Secondly, we should ensure that appointments of committee members are approved by the College of Physicians and Surgeons of the province concerned. This seems quite logical and normal to me. Why? Because when somebody wants to speak about freedom, one addresses himself to free men. The hospital committees, the doctors belonging to various Quebec associations-not only in the areas in which we are more particularly concerned, we, of the Ralliement creditiste, but throughout the province,-ask us to intervene, to go on fighting this battle which will end only when it is at last understood that there is an advantage for the country to suspend consideration of the litigious clauses of the omnibus bill.
May 2. 1969	COMMONS
It is not for nothing that every day we receive letters, phone calls, from the Canadian electorate. They tell us that they cannot address themselves to their member, because there is nothing he can do about this matter.
It is extremely unfortunate, Mr. Speaker, to find that such things can exist today. We are not surprised to see that one of the closest colleage of the Minister of Justice decided to depart from the policy of a party which deprived him of one of the most indefeasible rights one can enjoy, that is, the right to freedom.
When the electors find that their representative is not even free to express his opinion, it is unfortunate. It is a fact that is worth considering.
If this endless debate resulted only in having this bill amended rather radically, we would have gained something.
